## Data Analysis for BDE Report

In this markdown I explore the dataset of LinkedIn job postings from Kaggle.

```{r}
library(RKaggle)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

kaggleData <- get_dataset("arshkon/linkedin-job-postings")

```

# Data Exploration

Explore the data to see how it distributed/looks.

```{r}
# Put this at the top of your Data Exploration chunk (set to Inf for the full dataset)
# 2. Clean target variable (log annual USD base salary) and baseline controls

N_sample <- 20000

jobs <- kaggleData %>%
  filter(
    currency == "USD",
    compensation_type == "BASE_SALARY",
    pay_period %in% c("YEARLY", "HOURLY", "MONTHLY"),
    !is.na(normalized_salary),
    !is.na(description),
    nchar(description) > 100,                      # drop empty/stub ads
    normalized_salary >= 20000,                    # drops un-annualized hourly errors
    normalized_salary <= 500000                    # drops mis-multiplied scraping errors
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_wage = log(normalized_salary),
    full_text = paste(title, description),
    # Clean control variables (replace NAs with explicit categories)
    exp_level = replace_na(formatted_experience_level, "Not_Specified"),
    work_type = replace_na(formatted_work_type, "Not_Specified"),
    remote    = if_else(is.na(remote_allowed), 0L, 1L),
    # Extract 2-letter US state from strings like "Austin, TX"
    state     = replace_na(str_extract(location, ",\\s*([A-Z]{2})$", group = 1), "Other")
  ) %>%
  # Remove duplicate postings (same title + description) to avoid train/test leakage
  distinct(title, description, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Downsample to N_sample rows reproducibly
set.seed(42)
if (nrow(jobs) > N_sample) {
  jobs <- slice_sample(jobs, n = N_sample)
}

# Free the raw Kaggle table from RAM immediately
rm(kaggleData)
gc()

cat("Working sample size N:", nrow(jobs), "\n")
```

I remove the EEO Legal Boilerplate as well.

```{r}
library(quanteda)
library(Matrix)

binary <- FALSE

# 1. Unigram leakage & boilerplate (use * wildcards to catch all word forms before stemming)
leakage_words <- c(
  "salary", "salaries", "pay", "paid", "compensation", "base", "bonus", "bonuses",
  "usd", "dollar", "dollars", "hour", "hourly", "hr", "year", "years", "yearly", "yr",
  "annum", "annual", "annually", "month", "monthly", "week", "weekly", "k",
  "range", "rate", "rates", "ote", "commission", "commissions", "equity",
  "stipend", "401k", "401", "benefits", "competitive", "doe",
  "eeo", "discrimin*", "race", "religion", "citizenship", "opportun*", "unlaw*"
)

# 2. Tokenize and build unigrams + bigrams
toks <- corpus(jobs, text_field = "full_text") %>%
  tokens(remove_punct = TRUE, remove_numbers = TRUE, remove_symbols = TRUE, remove_url = TRUE) %>%
  tokens_tolower() %>%
  tokens_remove(c(stopwords("en"), leakage_words)) %>%
  tokens_wordstem() %>%
  tokens_ngrams(n = 1:2)

# 3. Build DTM, remove bigram scraping artifacts, and trim sparsity
dfm_mat <- dfm(toks) %>%
  dfm_remove(c("job_id", "job_detail", "job_shift")) %>%
  dfm_trim(min_docfreq = 0.01, max_docfreq = 0.80, docfreq_type = "prop")

# TF-IDF weighting (alternative: dfm_weight(dfm_mat, scheme = "boolean") for 0/1 presence)
if (binary == FALSE) {
  X_text <- dfm_tfidf(dfm_mat) %>% as("dgCMatrix")
} else {
  X_text_bin <- dfm_weight(dfm_mat, scheme = "boolean") %>% as("dgCMatrix")
}


# 4. Build sparse dummy matrix for controls (excluding intercept)
X_ctrl <- sparse.model.matrix(~ exp_level + work_type + remote + state, data = jobs)[, -1]

# Combine controls + text into one matrix
X_full <- cbind(X_ctrl, X_text)
y      <- jobs$log_wage

cat("Untrimmed DTM features:", ncol(dfm(toks)), "| Trimmed p:", ncol(X_full), "\n")

p_ctrl <- ncol(X_ctrl)
p_text <- ncol(X_text)
cat("Controls:", p_ctrl, "| Text features:", p_text, "| Total p:", ncol(X_full), "\n")
```

First penalised regression models.

```{r}
library(glmnet)
library(irlba)
library(Matrix)

set.seed(42)
train_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(X_full)), size = floor(0.8 * nrow(X_full)))

X_tr <- X_full[train_idx, ];  X_te <- X_full[-train_idx, ]
y_tr <- y[train_idx];         y_te <- y[-train_idx]

# Keep controls unpenalized (0), penalize text features (1)
pf_base <- c(rep(0, p_ctrl), rep(1, p_text))

# --- 0. Baseline OLS (Controls only) ---
ols_df_tr <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(X_ctrl[train_idx, ]))
ols_df_te <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(X_ctrl[-train_idx, ]))
fit_ols   <- lm(y_tr ~ ., data = ols_df_tr)
pred_ols  <- predict(fit_ols, newdata = ols_df_te)

# --- 0b. Full OLS (Unpenalized Controls + All Text Features) ---
fit_full_ols  <- glmnet(X_tr, y_tr, alpha = 0, lambda = 0)
pred_full_ols <- as.numeric(predict(fit_full_ols, newx = X_te))

# --- 1. Penalized Regressions (glmnet standardizes internally) ---
cv_ridge   <- cv.glmnet(X_tr, y_tr, alpha = 0,   penalty.factor = pf_base)
cv_lasso   <- cv.glmnet(X_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1,   penalty.factor = pf_base)
cv_elastic <- cv.glmnet(X_tr, y_tr, alpha = 0.5, penalty.factor = pf_base)

# Adaptive Lasso (Ridge initial weights on text columns)
ridge_coefs  <- as.numeric(coef(cv_ridge, s = "lambda.min"))[-1]
adapt_w_text <- 1 / (abs(ridge_coefs[(p_ctrl + 1):ncol(X_full)]) + 1e-7)
pf_adapt     <- c(rep(0, p_ctrl), adapt_w_text)
cv_adapt     <- cv.glmnet(X_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1, penalty.factor = pf_adapt)

pred_ridge   <- as.numeric(predict(cv_ridge,   s = "lambda.min", newx = X_te))
pred_lasso   <- as.numeric(predict(cv_lasso,   s = "lambda.min", newx = X_te))
pred_elastic <- as.numeric(predict(cv_elastic, s = "lambda.min", newx = X_te))
pred_adapt   <- as.numeric(predict(cv_adapt,   s = "lambda.min", newx = X_te))
```

Now factor models.

```{r}
# --- 2. Factor-Augmented Regression (Unsupervised PCA via irlba) ---
X_text_tr <- X_text[train_idx, ]
X_text_te <- X_text[-train_idx, ]

r_max   <- 50
pca_fit <- prcomp_irlba(X_text_tr, n = r_max, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
F_tr    <- pca_fit$x
F_te    <- predict(pca_fit, newdata = X_text_te)

r_opt   <- 30
fa_tr   <- cbind(ols_df_tr, as.data.frame(F_tr[, 1:r_opt]))
fa_te   <- cbind(ols_df_te, as.data.frame(F_te[, 1:r_opt]))
fit_fa  <- lm(y_tr ~ ., data = fa_tr)
pred_fa <- predict(fit_fa, newdata = fa_te)

# --- 3. NEW: Partial Least Squares (Supervised Sparse PLS1) ---
fit_sparse_pls <- function(X_train, y_train, X_test, ncomp = 30) {
  # Standardize using training mean & sd without densifying X
  mu <- Matrix::colMeans(X_train)
  sd <- sqrt(pmax(0, Matrix::colMeans(X_train^2) - mu^2))
  sd[sd == 0] <- 1
  
  Ax    <- function(v) { vs <- v / sd; as.numeric(X_train %*% vs) - sum(mu * vs) }
  Atx   <- function(u) { (as.numeric(Matrix::crossprod(X_train, u)) - sum(u) * mu) / sd }
  Ax_te <- function(v) { vs <- v / sd; as.numeric(X_test  %*% vs) - sum(mu * vs) }
  
  s <- Atx(y_train - mean(y_train))
  T_tr <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(X_train), ncol = ncomp)
  R_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = ncol(X_train), ncol = ncomp)
  V_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = ncol(X_train), ncol = ncomp)
  
  for (m in seq_len(ncomp)) {
    r <- s
    t_vec <- Ax(r)
    if (m > 1) {
      a_t   <- as.numeric(crossprod(T_tr[, 1:(m - 1), drop = FALSE], t_vec))
      t_vec <- t_vec - as.numeric(T_tr[, 1:(m - 1), drop = FALSE] %*% a_t)
      r     <- r     - as.numeric(R_mat[, 1:(m - 1), drop = FALSE] %*% a_t)
    }
    t_norm <- sqrt(sum(t_vec^2))
    t_vec  <- t_vec / t_norm
    r      <- r / t_norm
    T_tr[, m]  <- t_vec
    R_mat[, m] <- r
    
    v_vec <- Atx(t_vec)
    if (m > 1) {
      a_v   <- as.numeric(crossprod(V_mat[, 1:(m - 1), drop = FALSE], v_vec))
      v_vec <- v_vec - as.numeric(V_mat[, 1:(m - 1), drop = FALSE] %*% a_v)
    }
    v_vec <- v_vec / sqrt(sum(v_vec^2))
    V_mat[, m] <- v_vec
    s <- s - v_vec * sum(v_vec * s)
  }
  
  T_te <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(X_test), ncol = ncomp)
  for (m in seq_len(ncomp)) T_te[, m] <- Ax_te(R_mat[, m])
  
  colnames(T_tr) <- colnames(T_te) <- paste0("PLS_", seq_len(ncomp))
  list(T_tr = T_tr, T_te = T_te)
}

# --- 3. Partial Least Squares with 5-Fold CV to Select Optimal M ---
set.seed(42)
K      <- 5
m_grid <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30)
folds  <- sample(rep(seq_len(K), length.out = length(y_tr)))

cv_mspe <- matrix(0, nrow = K, ncol = length(m_grid))
colnames(cv_mspe) <- paste0("M=", m_grid)

for (k in seq_len(K)) {
  va_k <- which(folds == k)
  tr_k <- which(folds != k)
  
  # 1. Fit controls-only OLS inside the 4 training folds to get clean residuals
  ols_k <- lm(y_tr[tr_k] ~ ., data = ols_df_tr[tr_k, , drop = FALSE])
  
  # 2. Extract all max(m_grid) = 30 PLS directions ONCE for this fold
  pls_k <- fit_sparse_pls(
    X_train = X_text_tr[tr_k, ],
    y_train = resid(ols_k),
    X_test  = X_text_tr[va_k, ],
    ncomp   = max(m_grid)
  )
  
  # 3. Evaluate each candidate M on the held-out fold
  for (j in seq_along(m_grid)) {
    m <- m_grid[j]
    df_tr_m <- cbind(ols_df_tr[tr_k, , drop = FALSE], as.data.frame(pls_k$T_tr[, 1:m, drop = FALSE]))
    df_va_m <- cbind(ols_df_tr[va_k, , drop = FALSE], as.data.frame(pls_k$T_te[, 1:m, drop = FALSE]))
    
    mod_m  <- lm(y_tr[tr_k] ~ ., data = df_tr_m)
    pred_m <- suppressWarnings(predict(mod_m, newdata = df_va_m))
    cv_mspe[k, j] <- mean((pred_m - y_tr[va_k])^2)
  }
}

# Select M that minimizes 5-fold CV MSPE
mean_cv_mspe <- colMeans(cv_mspe)
m_opt        <- m_grid[which.min(mean_cv_mspe)]
print(round(mean_cv_mspe, 4))
cat("Optimal number of PLS components (M_opt):", m_opt, "\n")

# Refit PLS on the full training set using m_opt and evaluate on the test set
pls_full <- fit_sparse_pls(X_text_tr, resid(fit_ols), X_text_te, ncomp = m_opt)

fit_pls_cv  <- lm(y_tr ~ ., data = cbind(ols_df_tr, as.data.frame(pls_full$T_tr)))
pred_pls_cv <- predict(fit_pls_cv, newdata = cbind(ols_df_te, as.data.frame(pls_full$T_te)))

# --- 4. NEW: Hybrid Factor-Augmented Penalized Regression ---
# Combine controls + 30 PCA factors (unpenalized) + raw text terms (penalized)
X_hyb_tr <- cbind(X_ctrl[train_idx, ],  Matrix(F_tr[, 1:r_opt], sparse = TRUE), X_text_tr)
X_hyb_te <- cbind(X_ctrl[-train_idx, ], Matrix(F_te[, 1:r_opt], sparse = TRUE), X_text_te)

pf_hyb <- c(rep(0, p_ctrl), rep(0, r_opt), rep(1, p_text))

cv_hyb_lasso   <- cv.glmnet(X_hyb_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1,   penalty.factor = pf_hyb)
cv_hyb_elastic <- cv.glmnet(X_hyb_tr, y_tr, alpha = 0.5, penalty.factor = pf_hyb)

pred_hyb_lasso   <- as.numeric(predict(cv_hyb_lasso,   s = "lambda.min", newx = X_hyb_te))
pred_hyb_elastic <- as.numeric(predict(cv_hyb_elastic, s = "lambda.min", newx = X_hyb_te))
```

The performance table.

```{r}
# --- Evaluation Table (MSPE and Out-of-Sample R^2) ---
eval_model <- function(pred, actual) {
  mspe <- mean((pred - actual)^2)
  r2   <- 1 - sum((actual - pred)^2) / sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
  c(MSPE = mspe, OOS_R2 = r2)
}

results <- rbind(
  Baseline_OLS     = eval_model(pred_ols,         y_te),
  Full_OLS         = eval_model(pred_full_ols,    y_te),
  Factor_PCA_30    = eval_model(pred_fa,          y_te),
  Factor_PLS_CV    = eval_model(pred_pls_cv,      y_te),
  Ridge            = eval_model(pred_ridge,       y_te),
  Lasso            = eval_model(pred_lasso,       y_te),
  Elastic_Net      = eval_model(pred_elastic,     y_te),
  Adaptive_Lasso   = eval_model(pred_adapt,       y_te),
  Hybrid_FA_Lasso  = eval_model(pred_hyb_lasso,   y_te),
  Hybrid_FA_ENet   = eval_model(pred_hyb_elastic, y_te)
)

print(round(results, 4))
barplot(results[,1])
barplot(results[,2])

plot(m_grid, mean_cv_mspe, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of PLS Components (M)", ylab = "5-Fold CV MSPE",
     main = paste0("PLS Cross-Validation Error (Optimal M = ", m_opt, ")"))
abline(v = m_opt, col = "red", lty = 2)
```

```{r}
# 1. Count non-zero text coefficients (excluding intercept and controls)
count_nz <- function(cv_mod) {
  b <- as.numeric(coef(cv_mod, s = "lambda.min"))[-1]
  sum(b[(p_ctrl + 1):length(b)] != 0)
}

cat("Non-zero text terms -> Ridge:", count_nz(cv_ridge),
    "| Elastic Net:", count_nz(cv_elastic),
    "| Lasso:", count_nz(cv_lasso),
    "| Adaptive Lasso:", count_nz(cv_adapt), "\n")

# 2. Sanity check: inspect the top 15 positive and negative Lasso text coefficients
lasso_b <- as.numeric(coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.min"))[-1]
text_b  <- lasso_b[(p_ctrl + 1):length(lasso_b)]
names(text_b) <- colnames(X_text)

cat("\nTop 15 Highest-Wage Terms:\n")
print(round(sort(text_b, decreasing = TRUE)[1:15], 4))

cat("\nTop 15 Lowest-Wage Terms:\n")
print(round(sort(text_b, decreasing = FALSE)[1:15], 4))

```

Now again to see sparsity vs. prediction trade-off using s="lambda.1se" (1-standard-error rule)

```{r}
# Helper to evaluate any cv.glmnet object at "lambda.min" or "lambda.1se"
eval_cv <- function(cv_mod, s_rule) {
  pred <- as.numeric(predict(cv_mod, s = s_rule, newx = X_te))
  mspe <- mean((pred - y_te)^2)
  r2   <- 1 - sum((y_te - pred)^2) / sum((y_te - mean(y_te))^2)
  b    <- as.numeric(coef(cv_mod, s = s_rule))[-1]
  nz   <- sum(b[(p_ctrl + 1):length(b)] != 0)
  c(MSPE = round(mspe, 4), OOS_R2 = round(r2, 4), NonZero_Text = nz)
}

sparsity_tradeoff <- rbind(
  Lasso_min      = eval_cv(cv_lasso,   "lambda.min"),
  Lasso_1se      = eval_cv(cv_lasso,   "lambda.1se"),
  ElasticNet_min = eval_cv(cv_elastic, "lambda.min"),
  ElasticNet_1se = eval_cv(cv_elastic, "lambda.1se"),
  AdaptLasso_min = eval_cv(cv_adapt,   "lambda.min"),
  AdaptLasso_1se = eval_cv(cv_adapt,   "lambda.1se")
)

print(sparsity_tradeoff)
```

# Looking at Target Skills

```{r}
library(desla)
library(hdm)

# 1. Check which target skills exist in your stemmed DTM
candidates <- c("python", "sql", "excel", "cloud", "aws", "ai", "machin_learn",
                "manag", "leadership", "communic", "sale", "nurs", "account")
target_skills <- intersect(candidates, colnames(X_text))
print(target_skills)

# 2. For computational speed in desla, keep controls + top 500 text features (plus targets)
top_terms <- names(sort(colSums(X_text > 0), decreasing = TRUE))[1:500]
keep_text <- union(top_terms, target_skills)

if (binary == FALSE) {
  X_inf <- cbind(as.matrix(X_ctrl), as.matrix(X_text[, keep_text]))
} else {
  X_inf_bin  <- cbind(as.matrix(X_ctrl), as.matrix(X_text_bin[, keep_text]))
}

H_idx <- which(colnames(X_inf) %in% target_skills)

```

```{r}
# Runs valid high-dimensional inference on the columns in H_idx
ds_fit <- rlassoEffects(x = X_inf, y = y, index = H_idx)
summary(ds_fit)
confint(ds_fit)
```

If X_inf is TF-IDF: A coefficient of 0.0418 for python means a 1-unit increase in the TF-IDF score of "python" is associated with an approximate $+4.2\%$ higher wage. If X_inf is binary 0/1: You can interpret 0.0418 directly as an approximate $+4.27\%$ ($e^{0.0418} - 1$) wage premium for mentioning Python in the ad. Here it is TF-IDF.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Extract estimates, p-values, and 95% CIs from ds_fit
sum_tab <- summary(ds_fit)$coefficients
ci_tab  <- confint(ds_fit)

plot_df <- data.frame(
  raw_skill = rownames(sum_tab),
  estimate  = sum_tab[, "Estimate."],
  p_val     = sum_tab[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
  ci_low    = ci_tab[, 1],
  ci_high   = ci_tab[, 2],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 2. Map stemmed tokens to clean paper-ready labels
label_map <- c(
  python       = "Python",
  manag        = "Management",
  leadership   = "Leadership",
  machin_learn = "Machine Learning",
  sql          = "SQL",
  ai           = "AI",
  cloud        = "Cloud",
  nurs         = "Nursing",
  account      = "Accounting / Account",
  sale         = "Sales",
  communic     = "Communication",
  excel        = "Excel"
)

bonf_alpha <- 0.05 / nrow(plot_df)

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(
    label = ifelse(raw_skill %in% names(label_map), label_map[raw_skill], raw_skill),
    sig_group = case_when(
      p_val < bonf_alpha ~ "Significant (Bonferroni p < 0.0042)",
      p_val < 0.05       ~ "Significant (Nominal p < 0.05)",
      TRUE               ~ "Not Significant"
    ),
    sig_group = factor(sig_group, levels = c(
      "Significant (Bonferroni p < 0.0042)",
      "Significant (Nominal p < 0.05)",
      "Not Significant"
    ))
  )

# 3. Build the coefficient plot
p_skills <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(label, estimate), color = sig_group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high), height = 0.22, linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Significant (Bonferroni p < 0.0042)" = "#1B4F72",
    "Significant (Nominal p < 0.05)"      = "#D4AC0D",
    "Not Significant"                     = "#95A5A6"
  )) +
  labs(
    title    = "Estimated Log-Wage Premia of Selected Labor Market Skills",
    subtitle = "Double-Selection Lasso (rlassoEffects) with 95% Confidence Intervals",
    x        = "Estimated Effect on Log Annual Wage (per 1-unit TF-IDF)",
    y        = NULL,
    color    = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y       = element_text(color = "black", size = 10)
  )

print(p_skills)

# 4. Export high-resolution figure for your PDF paper
ggsave("skill_wage_premia.png", plot = p_skills, width = 7.5, height = 5, dpi = 300)
# Or PDF for LaTeX:
# ggsave("skill_wage_premia.pdf", plot = p_skills, width = 7.5, height = 5)
```

```{r}
# Extract raw estimates and p-values from your rlassoEffects object
res <- as.data.frame(summary(ds_fit)$coefficients)
colnames(res) <- c("Estimate", "SE", "t_stat", "p_raw")

# Apply multiple-testing adjustments across the M = 12 hypotheses
res$p_bonf <- p.adjust(res$p_raw, method = "bonferroni")
res$p_holm <- p.adjust(res$p_raw, method = "holm")

# Flag significance at the 5% level under each rule
res$sig_nominal <- res$p_raw  < 0.05
res$sig_bonf    <- res$p_bonf < 0.05
res$sig_holm    <- res$p_holm < 0.05

# Sort from smallest to largest raw p-value
res <- res[order(res$p_raw), ]
print(res[, c("Estimate", "p_raw", "p_bonf", "p_holm", "sig_bonf", "sig_holm")], digits = 4)
```

```{r}
print(round(ci_joint, 4))
```

Try Tree-Guided Aggregation with glmnet instead of rare

```{r}
library(glmnet)
library(Matrix)

# Helper: build the p x (2p - 1) sparse tree descendant matrix A from hclust()
build_tree_matrix <- function(hc) {
  p <- length(hc$order)
  m <- nrow(hc$merge) # p - 1 internal nodes
  desc <- vector("list", p + m)
  for (j in seq_len(p)) desc[[j]] <- j
  for (k in seq_len(m)) {
    left  <- hc$merge[k, 1]
    right <- hc$merge[k, 2]
    idx_l <- if (left  < 0) -left  else p + left
    idx_r <- if (right < 0) -right else p + right
    desc[[p + k]] <- c(desc[[idx_l]], desc[[idx_r]])
  }
  i_idx <- unlist(desc)
  j_idx <- rep(seq_along(desc), lengths(desc))
  list(
    A    = sparseMatrix(i = i_idx, j = j_idx, x = 1, dims = c(p, p + m)),
    desc = desc
  )
}

# 1. Select top 500 text terms (plus target skills) strictly from training data
top_500   <- names(sort(colSums(X_text_tr > 0), decreasing = TRUE))[1:500]
tree_cols <- union(top_500, target_skills)

X_tree_tr <- X_text_tr[, tree_cols]
X_tree_te <- X_text_te[, tree_cols]

# 2. Build hierarchical clustering tree on TRAINING features only
cor_mat  <- cor(as.matrix(X_tree_tr))
hc_tree  <- hclust(as.dist(1 - cor_mat), method = "average")
tree_obj <- build_tree_matrix(hc_tree)
A_mat    <- tree_obj$A

# 3. Form aggregated tree features Z = X * A (leaves + all internal branches)
Z_tr <- X_tree_tr %*% A_mat
Z_te <- X_tree_te %*% A_mat

# Combine unpenalized controls W with penalized tree features Z
X_tag_tr <- cbind(X_ctrl[train_idx, ],  Z_tr)
X_tag_te <- cbind(X_ctrl[-train_idx, ], Z_te)
pf_tag   <- c(rep(0, p_ctrl), rep(1, ncol(Z_tr)))

# 4. Fit Tree-Guided Aggregation via 10-fold CV in glmnet
set.seed(42)
cv_tree_agg   <- cv.glmnet(X_tag_tr, y_tr, alpha = 1, penalty.factor = pf_tag)
pred_tree_agg <- as.numeric(predict(cv_tree_agg, s = "lambda.min", newx = X_tag_te))

# Evaluate for your horse race table
print(round(eval_model(pred_tree_agg, y_te), 4))
```

Inspect.

```{r}
p_sub     <- length(tree_cols)
gamma_hat <- as.numeric(coef(cv_tree_agg, s = "lambda.1se"))[-1][(p_ctrl + 1):ncol(X_tag_tr)]

# Internal nodes (branches with >= 2 fused words) that are non-zero
active_branches <- which(gamma_hat != 0 & seq_along(gamma_hat) > p_sub)
cat("Active fused branches (at lambda.1se):", length(active_branches), "\n\n")

# Sort by largest absolute effect and print top 10 clusters
top_branches <- active_branches[order(abs(gamma_hat[active_branches]), decreasing = TRUE)]
for (b in head(top_branches, 10)) {
  words <- tree_cols[tree_obj$desc[[b]]]
  if (length(words) <= 15) { # skip huge near-root branches for readability
    cat(sprintf("Gamma = %+.4f | Words (%d): %s\n",
                gamma_hat[b], length(words), paste(words, collapse = ", ")))
  }
}
```
